title: Deepfake videos of PM Lee and DPM Wong promote crypto and investment scams
summary: Fake videos using the likeness of Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong, and separately Deputy PM Lawrence Wong, were used to promote cryptocurrency and investment schemes. The date is PM Lee's public warning, the earliest public record found; the videos had been circulating for some days.

title: Second deepfake of Lee Hsien Loong promotes an investment product
summary: A new deepfake showed Lee Hsien Loong, by then Senior Minister, endorsing an investment product with guaranteed returns. He warned the public again.
notes: Exact day not confirmed from a primary source.

title: Deepfake videos and voice clones of PM Lawrence Wong promote scams
summary: AI-generated video and a cloned voice of Prime Minister Wong were used to promote cryptocurrency, money-making schemes and PR services.

title: Grok image-tool misuse (sexualised deepfakes): Singapore exposure
summary: From late December 2025 the Grok chatbot on X was widely used to produce non-consensual sexualised edits of real people. The sources checked do not quantify local complaints in Singapore. The case is included because the service was available and the regulator engaged X.
notes: Onset date is the start of a documented analysis window of mass misuse; sources vary on the exact start. Local harm not quantified.

title: Grok image-tool misuse (sexualised deepfakes): Indonesia
summary: Reports that Grok produced sexualised images of real women and minors led Indonesia's communications ministry to begin investigating in early January 2026.
source_title: Marketing-Interactive on IMDA and regional action
notes: Same onset rule as the other Grok cases.

title: Deepfakes of President Prabowo and Finance Minister Sri Mulyani used in fake aid scams
summary: Fraudsters used AI-generated videos of senior officials to promise cash aid and collect fees through WhatsApp. One suspect reportedly took about Rp65 million from around 100 victims from December 2024. The OECD incident monitor records a related scam across 20 provinces.
notes: Onset is 'since December 2024' per the source, so lags are approximate.

title: Deepfake of Finance Minister Sri Mulyani calling teachers a 'burden'
summary: A manipulated clip cut from her 7 August 2025 speech falsely showed the minister calling teachers a burden on the state. An official later said false content had fuelled anger and protests; that causal link is the official's claim and is not independently established here.
notes: Date is the minister's own denial, the earliest public record found.

title: Deepfake news-anchor and PM videos promote investment schemes on Facebook
summary: AI-manipulated videos imitating Bernama TV news anchors, and a fake clip of PM Anwar Ibrahim, promoted dubious investment schemes on Facebook after repeated incidents. Earlier circulation is likely, so this is a running series and not a single dated event.
notes: Onset unknown, so no response lag is computed for this series.

title: Grok image-tool misuse (sexualised deepfakes): Malaysia
summary: MCMC recorded 17 complaints or reports about Grok misuse in Malaysia: six formal complaints, two police reports, eight social-media tagging complaints and one First Information Report opened by MCMC. Content involved women and minors.

title: Deepfake audio of President Marcos 'ordering' military action
summary: Manipulated audio imitating President Marcos appeared to direct the armed forces to act against a foreign country, during South China Sea tensions and a joint military exercise. Officials said the clip was fake and probably produced by a foreign actor.
notes: Date is the first official statement, the earliest public record found.

title: Grok image-tool misuse (sexualised deepfakes): Philippines
summary: Authorities cited Grok's capacity to generate sexually explicit, non-consensual deepfake material, including content that could involve minors.

title: Deepfake video-call impersonation scams
summary: Scammers took over Zalo and Facebook accounts and used the owners' photos and videos to stage fake video calls asking contacts for money.
notes: Date is the earliest report found.

title: Deepfake sextortion of individuals and entrepreneurs
summary: Criminals used face-swapped explicit videos to extort victims, including a Hanoi schoolgirl in March 2024 and entrepreneurs in Ho Chi Minh City in early 2024.

title: Deepfake Zoom call impersonating PM Wong and other officials costs a victim at least S$4.9 million
summary: Scammers contacted a business professional on WhatsApp, posing as the Secretary to the Cabinet, and invited him to a fabricated Zoom meeting featuring AI-generated versions of the Prime Minister, the President and other officials. He transferred at least S$4.9 million before realising on 14 May 2026 that it was fake. The date is the Singapore Police Force advisory; the scam began earlier.
notes: Onset unknown (the money moved in several transfers before 14 May), so no response lag is computed. Also cited in TFGI's Perspectives series on AI readiness (10 Nov 2026).

title: Thai PM targeted by an AI voice-clone scam impersonating another leader
summary: Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra said she received a realistic voice message mimicking a well-known ASEAN leader, whom she did not name, asking for a donation and claiming Thailand was the only member yet to contribute. She said she nearly fell for it. The date is her public account; the call came earlier.
notes: The date of the call itself is not stated in the sources checked, so no response lag is computed.

title: AI face-altering video-call scam impersonating police, run from a Poipet call centre
summary: A call-centre gang operating from Poipet, Cambodia, impersonated Thai police on video calls and used AI to alter the callers' faces. Police said it targeted at least 163 people; one victim, a Thai-British beauty queen, lost 4 million baht. Thailand's Central Investigation Bureau arrested two suspects on 2 and 3 February 2025.
notes: The date is the arrests, the first public record, so the scam itself was earlier and undated. The Star reports the two suspects said they were forced to work for the gang.

title: AI-generated 'pilot' persona lures a 66-year-old woman to Chiang Mai airport
summary: A 66-year-old woman from Lampang travelled alone to Chiang Mai International Airport to meet a man she believed was a pilot, then learned he was an AI-generated character on Facebook. The OECD monitor classifies the harm as psychological; the sources listed do not report a financial loss.
source_title: OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor, 17 Sep 2026
notes: Underlying Bangkok Post article (17 Sep 2026) read in full 22 Nov 2026: a 66-year-old woman from Lampang travelled to Chiang Mai airport on the evening of 16 Sep to meet a man she believed was a pilot; officers concluded his photo appeared AI-generated and posted on Facebook. No financial loss reported. No official response found.

title: Deepfake videos of JG Summit CEO Lance Gokongwei used to promote fake crypto and forex schemes
summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission warned that scammers were using deepfake video and audio of Lance Gokongwei, president and CEO of JG Summit Holdings, to endorse fraudulent crypto and forex investments. The date is the SEC warning, the earliest public record found.
source_title: AI Incident Database 1148 (reports on the SEC warning)
notes: Verified from the incident-database entry; the SEC advisory itself was not opened. Onset unknown.

title: AI-assisted romance scams using deepfake personas draw police and CICC alerts
summary: The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) and the Philippine National Police issued alerts about AI-assisted romance scams, in which scammers use AI-generated personas. The civil-society group Scam Watch Pilipinas cited a retired school principal who lost 2.5 million pesos. This is a running series, not one dated event.
notes: Underlying articles read in full 22 Nov 2026: Philstar and PhilstarLife (both 4 Feb 2026) confirm the PNP Anti-Cybercrime Group and CICC warnings about AI-assisted love scams and deepfake personas; SecurityMatters (12 Feb 2026, citing PIA) confirms the Scam Watch Pilipinas case of a retired principal who lost ₱2.5 million. The PNP/CICC 'Red Alert' was issued 4 Feb 2026.

title: Deepfake Zoom call impersonating company executives costs a finance director over US$499,000
summary: A finance director of a multinational was contacted on WhatsApp on 24 Mar 2025 by a scammer posing as the CFO, then joined a Zoom call on 25 Mar in which the CEO and other executives were impersonated using deepfake technology. He transferred over US$499,000 (~S$670,000) on 26 Mar 2025; the scam was discovered on 27 Mar and Singapore/Hong Kong police withheld/seized the funds on 28 Mar.
notes: Date is first contact (24 Mar) per the SPF release of 7 Apr 2025, the earliest public record found; transfer 26 Mar, discovery 27 Mar, recovery 28 Mar. No OECD AIM entry found for this case; the OECD entry 2026-05-14-1081 is the different S$4.9m case (SG-I-05). SPF/MAS/CSA issued a joint advisory on 12 Mar 2025 warning of exactly this scam variant; it predates the incident, so it is recorded here, not as a response row.

title: Deepfake nude photos of students at a Singapore sports school created and shared by classmates
summary: Male students at a Singapore sports school generated and circulated deepfake nude images of female schoolmates from June 2024, using two WhatsApp groups (one to generate, one to circulate). The case became public on 12 Nov 2024. The school lodged a police report and disciplined students involved, including caning, suspension and sports-trip bans.
notes: Onset month from a victim's parent via CNA ('dates back to June'); exact start day unknown. No OECD AIM entry found for this case. Students aged 13-18. School not named in the tracker text: schools are not named in sexual-deepfake cases involving minors (the school name stays in the source link).

title: Deepfake sextortion emails target over 100 public servants including five ministers
summary: From 26 Nov 2024, more than 100 civil servants across 31 government agencies, including 12 political office-holders / five ministers, received extortion emails with fake compromising photos of themselves, demanding US$50,000 in cryptocurrency. No monetary loss was reported. MDDI confirmed the incident and police were investigating.
notes: MDDI statement as reported 29 Nov 2024; the primary MDDI statement itself was not opened.

title: Deepfake video of President Jokowi speaking Mandarin
summary: AI-manipulated video falsely showed President Joko Widodo delivering a speech in Mandarin (the original was a 2015 speech in English). It circulated in October 2023 ahead of the 2024 presidential election. Kominfo debunked it on 26 October 2023, explaining how the deepfake was produced. Date is the Kominfo debunk, the earliest verified public record found; the video circulated earlier in October.
source_title: Blackbird.AI: Deepfakes in the Indonesian election
notes: OECD AIM lists this as a hazard (2023-12-05-b2db). Kominfo debunk date 26 Oct 2023 from Verihubs and the DKPP journal bibliography; the CNN Indonesia page itself could not be opened.

title: AI-generated nude images of 300+ female students at a Seremban secondary school
summary: A Form Five student allegedly used AI to generate explicit deepfake images of female schoolmates, stored on his phone and circulated among students, allegedly sold via Telegram. Discovered 12 Aug 2026 when a Form Two student found the phone in the school surau; five police reports lodged 20-23 Aug 2026; school confirmed 300+ victims on 15 Sep 2026. Date is the first public reporting (The Star, 17 Oct 2026).
source_title: Media Selangor, 19 Oct 2026 (reporting Harian Metro; see also The Star, 17 Oct 2026)
notes: OECD AIM has two entries for this case (2026-10-15-dc0c and 2026-10-18-8df8); treat as one incident. Source switched 22 Nov 2026 from the AI Risk Wire aggregator (machine-generated, unverified) to Media Selangor (19 Oct 2026, reporting Harian Metro), which supports the 300+ victims, Telegram circulation/sale, 12 Aug discovery, five reports 20-23 Aug and 15 Sep confirmation; the victims' ages and the 'around 200 images' figure could not be verified against an accessible source and were removed.

title: 713 AI-generated deepfake posts targeting political leaders removed since January 2025
summary: Malaysian authorities removed 713 AI-generated deepfake social media posts targeting political leaders, following public complaints and legal violations. MCMC coordinated the takedowns. This is a running series from January 2025, not a single dated event; date is the OECD AIM entry date.
notes: Onset unknown, so no response lag. Overlaps thematically with MY-I-01 (investment-scam deepfakes of leaders) but is a distinct official count of political-leader deepfakes; kept separate.

title: Claude-powered commercial election-manipulation platform targeting Malaysian voters
summary: Anthropic's threat report (10 Sep 2026) disclosed case GTG-84005: an Istanbul-based firm, BBS Bilisim Teknolojileri, allegedly used Claude to build a commercial election-manipulation platform targeting Malaysian users — voter profiling across all 222 parliamentary constituencies using census/electoral data, ~1,000 fake X accounts, a fake news site (Malaysia Pulse) and a YouTube channel. Anthropic terminated the Claude accounts. The firm denied involvement. Anthropic found no evidence the campaign reached genuine online communities. Operation ran Dec 2025-Aug 2026 per the report.
source_title: Marketing-Interactive: MCMC presses Anthropic over alleged Malaysia election manipulation
notes: Date is the Anthropic report publication (10 Sep 2026); OECD AIM dates the incident 11 Sep 2026. The underlying Anthropic report was not opened; facts rest on secondary reporting of it.

title: Deepfake video impersonating Border Control Agency (AKPS) director-general
summary: AI-generated deepfake video falsely depicted the director-general of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), aiming to damage his reputation and mislead the public. AKPS confirmed the video was fake, warned the public and announced potential legal action.
notes: AIM summary only; the underlying article was not opened. The second AIM entry (2025-12-07-ca89) is confirmed as a distinct incident — see MY-I-08 (two TikTok videos, 7 Dec 2025, false aid-support claims).

title: AI deepfake scam impersonating Johor state executive councillor on TikTok
summary: Multiple TikTok accounts used AI-generated images and voice to impersonate Johor state executive councillor Khairin-Nisa Ismail, promoting a fake aid scheme to steal personal data. Authorities shut down 12 accounts and are investigating.
notes: Response now recorded: MCMC took down the 12 accounts; announced by Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad on 24 Feb 2026 — see MY-R-15. Police report lodged by Khairin-Nisa Ismail on 20 Feb 2026; some accounts active since 9 Feb 2026. Four of the 12 accounts used her face and voice via AI.

title: Philippine officials share Veo 3-generated video of fake students opposing Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment
summary: A Veo 3-generated video styled as a street interview showed two AI-invented schoolboys opposing the impeachment of VP Sara Duterte. Posted on Facebook 14 Jun 2025, it was shared by Senator Ronald dela Rosa on 15 Jun and by Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte; it reached millions of views. The video depicts invented people, not a real person's likeness. A second Veo clip (an AI elderly fish-vendor arguing for impeachment) also circulated.
notes: Date is the original Facebook post (14 Jun); sharing by officials was 15 Jun. No OECD AIM entry found for this incident despite targeted searches; the 16 Jun 2025 backlog date appears to be the PCO response date.

title: AI deepfake video falsely shows Đồng Nai teacher crying over alleged sale of students' milk
summary: AI-generated deepfake videos falsely depicting a teacher crying after allegedly selling students' milk were widely shared on social media, causing public confusion and reputational harm. Police confirmed the videos were fabricated using AI.
notes: Date is the AIM listing date; confirm onset from the underlying article. Theme online-safety (synthetic-media misinformation/reputational harm) — no exact tracker theme fits; political-deepfakes was considered and rejected.

title: AI deepfake extortion scheme targets officials in Thanh Hóa
summary: In Thanh Hóa, nearly 20 individuals including government officials were targeted by extortionists using AI-assisted technology to create fake, sensitive images and videos; victims were threatened with public exposure unless large sums were paid, causing psychological distress and financial harm. (OECD AIM listing date; onset unconfirmed.)
notes: Date is the AIM listing date; onset unconfirmed — the underlying VietReader article (4 Oct 2026, read in full 22 Nov 2026) reports Thanh Hóa police disclosing on 4 Oct that they had received multiple reports from victims, with demands up to VND 1.5 billion, but gives no earlier dated record of when the extortion began. No police action beyond the warning is recorded.

title: AI deepfake extortion and fraud crackdown: cross-border rings targeting officials and businesspeople
summary: Vietnamese authorities disrupted criminal groups using AI-powered deepfake technology to fabricate sensitive images for extortion and fraud; investigations revealed cross-border networks involving Chinese nationals and local operatives targeting public officials and businesspeople through biometric spoofing, prompting coordinated raids across several provinces.
notes: Date is the AIM listing date; confirm onset from the underlying article. The crackdown itself is also the response — see VN-R-08.

title: Deepfake of Thai PBS World anchor and Miss Universe CEO promotes fake investment
summary: A purported AI deepfake impersonated Thai PBS World anchor Doliyana Bunnak interviewing Miss Universe Organization CEO Anne Jakkraphong Jakrajutatip, inviting investment from 8,000 baht with promised returns of hundreds of thousands. Thai PBS Verify found it fake; the underlying footage was from the 24 June 2025 Thai PBS World Tonight broadcast.
notes: Date is the original broadcast date per AIID; Thai PBS Verify publication date not confirmed in sources opened. No government/regulator response found.

title: Deepfake 'Crystallum AI' investment ad impersonates Thai PBS World anchors and business figures
summary: A Facebook ad misusing the Thai PBS World Tonight logo showed an anchor (former NHK World anchor Patchari Raksawong, who never anchored for Thai PBS) interviewing Central Group's Tos Chirathivat and Kalin Sarasin, promoting 'CRYSTALLUM AI' with a promised fivefold return. Thai PBS Verify traced the footage to a 2013 NHK flood report; HIVE Moderation gave a 72.3% probability of AI generation.
notes: Thai PBS Verify is a media fact-check, not a government response; Central Group's warning is corporate. No government/regulator response found.

title: AI sexual deepfakes of Semarang high-school students and teacher spread on X; maker later convicted
summary: AI-edited pornographic photos and videos using the faces of female students and at least one teacher of a Semarang high school spread on X from the account of an 18-year-old university student and alumnus: 300+ posts and 1,100 files stored. Victims included students, alumni and teaching staff.
notes: Onset is the 20 Oct 2025 Kompas report date, the earliest public record found; the posts began earlier in October. School not named in the tracker text: schools are not named in sexual-deepfake cases involving minors (the school name stays in the source link).

title: World App iris-scan biometric collection halted by privacy regulator
summary: Tools for Humanity's World App collected iris biometrics via Orb verification in the Philippines, incentivising scans with monetary rewards. The National Privacy Commission found the processing violated the Data Privacy Act and ordered it halted.
notes: Date is the cease-and-desist order, the earliest verified public record; the launch date was not verified, so onset_certainty is unknown.

title: Deepfake video of former president Halimah Yacob criticising the government circulates ahead of GE2025
summary: A deepfake video falsely showed former president Halimah Yacob making negative statements about the government, including a cloned voice. She said on 15 April 2025 she would file a police report.
notes: Whether the police report was actually filed is not confirmed. Halimah was not a candidate, so ELIONA's application to this clip is unclear.

title: Deepfake videos red-tag Makabayan bloc candidates as NPA recruiters during 2025 campaign
summary: Facebook pages posted AI deepfake videos depicting Makabayan candidates (including France Castro, Sarah Jane Elago, Teddy Casiño) as recruiters for the New People's Army, alongside manipulated audio. A 31 Jan video's audio scored 1/100 on a deepfake voice-detection tool. Castro appealed to COMELEC and DICT on 11 March 2025 to remove the videos.
notes: No specific COMELEC/DICT action on the 11 March appeal was found, so no response row is proposed. The general DICT-COMELEC Threat Monitoring Center is not tied to this complaint.

title: Deepfake romance-scam network fugitives arrested in Da Nang
summary: Three South Korean nationals who allegedly ran a Bavet-based romance-scam network using deepfakes to pose as women online were arrested in Da Nang after fleeing Cambodia on Interpol Red Notices. The network allegedly scammed about US$1 million between August and December 2024.
notes: Date is the arrest (28 Oct 2025); earliest public record is the police statement reported 5 Dec 2025. Scam activity itself was Aug-Dec 2024.

title: Deepfake ads impersonate Finance Minister Ekniti to promote investments
summary: AI-generated clips cloning the face and voice of Deputy PM and Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas circulated on Facebook and YouTube promoting investment schemes and loan apps falsely claiming Finance Ministry endorsement.
notes: Secondary sources citing Thaiger/Thairath/THE STANDARD; primary Thai reports not opened.

title: AI-generated video of Senate President Hun Sen falsely soliciting funds to wage war against Thailand
summary: Deepfake video repurposing footage of Hun Sen's 27 June meeting with civil servants in Preah Vihear, with a fabricated AI Thai voice track in which he purportedly asks viewers to transfer 300 baht via TrueMoney to fund a military force against Thailand, promising 50,000 baht in return.
notes: 27 June is the date AIID assigns and the date of the original Preah Vihear meeting whose footage was reused; AIID's own text says only that the video surfaced in late June 2025, so the exact circulation day is unconfirmed. Original news article behind Report 5442 (captioned 'MPTC condemns deepfake video of Senate President') could not be located despite targeted searches, so the MPTC statement's exact date is also unconfirmed.

title: AI-generated fake video imitating Prime Minister Hun Manet's voice
summary: Facebook account used AI to create a fake video imitating Prime Minister Hun Manet's voice to spread a message contrary to the truth.
notes: FreeLibrary reprint of the same Khmer Times article is dated 14 Nov 2025 (likely print date); Khmer Times online/Telegram and the AI Forum Cambodia newsletter cite 13 Nov 2025, which is used here.

title: Man arrested for using AI-generated fake news and images to solicit charitable donations
summary: A Siem Reap man allegedly used AI to create fake news and AI-produced images of orphans, and fabricated stories including fundraising for military heroes at the Cambodia-Thailand border and a grieving widow unable to afford a coffin, to solicit donations via five Facebook accounts with QR codes.
notes: 8 July is the arrest date stated by the Anti-Technology Crime Department; the fabricated posts themselves are undated, so onset is approximate. First published report found is 10 July 2025. Single-outlet account (Phnom Penh Post, reprinted in full by The Free Library).

title: AI-enabled impersonation scam calls from Laos target Spain; 3 million calls over nine months
summary: A Chinese criminal organisation used AI and phone spoofing to impersonate police and authorities, making three million scam calls from Laos to Spain over nine months; victims were deceived into transferring funds.
source_title: OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor, 10 Jul 2026
notes: Date is the AIM entry date; the underlying press article was not retrievable from the AIM page in this sweep. The nine-month call window implies activity from about October 2025. No Lao official response specifically to the Spain case was found; the linked responses are the Lao government's 2026 crackdown on the same scam-centre phenomenon.

title: ChatGPT used by forced labourers in KK Park scam compound to impersonate Americans in crypto investment scams
summary: Trafficked workers held at KK Park, Myawaddy, on the Myanmar-Thai border were forced to use ChatGPT to craft messages impersonating Americans and trick US victims, including real estate agents, into bogus cryptocurrency investments (pig-butchering scams); other workers used it for romance scams.
notes: Reuters states it could not independently verify the full details of the survivor's account. Date is publication date; ChatGPT use predates it (survivor left KK Park in Apr 2025; other workers report use from 2022). Text impersonation via ChatGPT, not a video or voice deepfake; themed general-ai.

title: AI-generated fake news misusing Brunei Darussalam Central Bank name and logo
summary: AI-generated fake news misusing the name and logo of the Brunei Darussalam Central Bank circulated on social media, using clickbait headlines to harvest personal or financial information, promote unlicensed financial products and services, and trick victims into installing malicious apps.
notes: BDCB's own site lists the press release 'Beware and Stay Alert of Fake News Generated By Artificial Intelligence (AI)' dated 14 June 2024; the RTB text confirms the warning followed recent AI-generated fake news misusing BDCB's name and logo. Exact first circulation date of the fake news is unknown, hence onset approximate.

title: Deepfake videos impersonating Royal Brunei Police Force officers promote 'Real Money Magic' investment scam
summary: Short AI-manipulated videos and audio impersonating Royal Brunei Police Force officers circulated on TikTok, Facebook and Instagram; several videos from a single TikTok account promoted a fraudulent investment scheme called 'Real Money Magic', falsely claiming it could solve financial problems with guaranteed quick profits.
source_title: Pasukan Polis Diraja Brunei (Royal Brunei Police Force), 13 Jul 2025
notes: AIID dates this incident 14 July 2025, apparently following the Borneo Bulletin report; the RBPF statement itself is dated Sunday 13 July 2025, the earliest public record found. The RBPF's Malay text renders the scheme name as 'nyata kemunculan wang ajaib'.

title: AI-generated fake article promoting 'BTC 800 Lurotix' crypto scheme misuses Brunei Darussalam Central Bank name
summary: An AI-generated fake article promoting a non-existent crypto-investment platform called 'BTC 800 Lurotix' circulated, misusing the Brunei Darussalam Central Bank's name; it claimed limited daily registrations, a verification call from a Bruneian account manager and a mandatory BND 250 deposit, framed as a way to bypass impending government blocks after a scandal involving RTB Perdana.
notes: Incident date is the date of BDCB's debunk post; the fake article circulated before that and its exact first appearance is unknown. Content details per the search-indexed summaries of the official BDCB and Waspada.bn Instagram posts; the posts themselves were not opened directly.

title: AI-generated fake video impersonating Brunei Darussalam Central Bank senior officials promotes investment scheme
summary: A fraudulent AI-manipulated video falsely claiming the Brunei Darussalam Central Bank promotes an investment scheme circulated; the video impersonated senior officials, and BDCB clarified it does not offer financial products or endorse schemes.
source_title: Brunei Darussalam Central Bank press release, 30 Jul 2026
notes: One search-indexed summary gives the Instagram post date as 29 July 2026; the post is listed as 30 July 2026 and the press release is cited as 30 Jul 2026, so 30 July is used. The press-release PDF could not be fetched (network error); content per BDCB's own publications page and its verified Instagram post.

title: AI-generated fake videos of Royal Brunei Police Force officers go viral on TikTok
summary: Viral AI-generated fake videos depicting Royal Brunei Police Force officers were uploaded via two TikTok accounts and widely viewed; police warned the videos were false and made with AI and cautioned against similar videos on Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Telegram.
source_title: Pasukan Polis Diraja Brunei (Royal Brunei Police Force), 9 Oct 2026
notes: The 9 Oct 2026 RBPF statement does not specify what the videos promoted; the same-day RBPF Instagram warning frames such fake TikTok accounts using AI videos of police officers as scams offering money or assistance via WhatsApp, which supports the deepfake-fraud theme. Exact first upload date unknown, hence onset approximate.

title: Deepfake videos impersonating AKPS director-general falsely claim support for aid programmes
summary: Two viral TikTok videos showing a face and voice resembling AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain falsely expressed support for certain aid programmes. AKPS denied the videos' authenticity, warned the public and said legal action would be taken. Distinct from MY-I-06 (6 Aug 2025): that was a single video by TikTok user 'Hermano Kedutaan' about passport documentation issues, aimed at damaging the DG's reputation; this is two videos, four months later, with false aid-support claims.
notes: Distinct from MY-I-06: different date (7 Dec vs 6 Aug 2025), different claims (aid-programme support vs passport documentation), two videos vs one. Date is the Bernama report date, the earliest public record found.

title: AI deepfake videos impersonate director Lý Hải and his wife to promote unverified health products
summary: AI-generated videos and audio impersonating director Lý Hải and his wife promoted tonics, supplements and other unverified products; Lý Hải warned on 1 May 2026 that the fakes were sophisticated enough to deceive viewers, especially older people, into fraudulent purchases. He had previously warned about the same impersonation in June 2025.
notes: Date is Lý Hải's 1 May 2026 warning, the earliest public record found; the videos had been circulating before that. No financial-loss figure verified. No response row: the AIM summary's 'authorities have intervened in some cases' names no authority, date or action; the only verifiable intervention found (HCMC police summoning two people, 8 Jan 2026) concerns the separate Quyền Linh fake-arrest videos (AIM 2025-12-08-ef7a), not this incident.

title: Ring sold nearly 1,000 bank accounts and used facial-data forgery software to defeat bank biometric checks (Thanh Hóa)
summary: A ring bought, collected and resold nearly 1,000 bank accounts; it used software that hijacked the phone camera and injected the account holder's stored portrait photo or video into bank facial-biometric checks, so the accounts could be operated without the holder present. The accounts were used to pay for gambling, money laundering and illicit advertising.
notes: Date is the 26 Jun 2026 report; the bust is described only as recent, exact day not stated. METHOD CAVEAT: sources describe a camera-hijack tool injecting stored portrait photos (Vietstock: software builds a video from the holder's photos); they do not call the tool itself AI. The deepfake framing comes from OECD AIM 2026-11-03-d510 and the 4 Nov 2026 National Assembly debate, where a delegate cited this exact Thanh Hóa case while warning about deepfake biometric fraud. Do NOT carry over the 14-member gang / VND 1 trillion / $38.4m figures: those belong to a different June 2025 case (Ninh Binh/Hanoi police, Phạm Hồng Chuyên; Biometric Update 2 Jun 2025), and the >VND 1 trillion / 1m-account figures belong to the separate May 2025 Thai Binh KUBET case (21 arrested). Name of the alleged ringleader withheld: private individual, accused not convicted, no official source names him. Counts follow the Vietstock/VietNamNet report ('nearly 1,000' accounts); the Sep 2025–Jun 2026 period and profit figures appear only in the non-official Cafebiz republication and are not used.

title: AI deepfake videos falsely claim TV host MC Quyền Linh has been arrested
summary: AI-generated videos and audio falsely claiming that television host MC Quyền Linh had been arrested by Ho Chi Minh City police circulated on social media in early December 2025. Quyền Linh denied the claim the same evening, saying the clips had been edited with AI. Police technical analysis later confirmed the material was AI-generated, combining fabricated images and audio.
notes: Date is the 8 Dec 2025 report of the fake-arrest videos; the underlying clips circulated earlier in December 2025. Quyền Linh is a public figure and the victim; naming him is consistent with the audit rules. The two people later summoned by police are not named (private individuals, warned not convicted).

title: Man in Madiun used ChatGPT to plan a murder and conceal the bodies
summary: A man in Madiun, East Java, used ChatGPT to research killing methods, plan how to dispose of the bodies and prepare answers for police questioning before murdering his common-law wife and her four-year-old child on 20 September 2026. Police revealed the ChatGPT use in early November 2026; the suspect had been arrested on 25 October 2026 in Jombang and was charged with premeditated murder.
source_title: OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor, 1 Nov 2026
notes: Date is the OECD AIM listing date, when the ChatGPT link became public; the murders occurred on 20 Sep 2026 and the arrest on 25 Oct 2026. The suspect and the victims are not named (suspect accused of murder, not convicted; victims are private individuals). Police disclosed on 4 Nov 2026 that the suspect had used ChatGPT to prepare scenarios and answers for questioning (Kompas, 5 Nov 2026).
